# Module CT — Discrete RECD Time versus Classical Continuous Thermodynamic Time

**Status:** mathematical confrontation module (statement-level)  
**Notation:** Systemic Tau monorepo (`τ_s`, `g`, `δ`, `T_n`, `Δt_k`)  
**Lean alignment:** `SystemicTau.RECD`, `SystemicTau.Thresholds`, `SystemicTau.Basic` (0 `sorry`, 0 research `axiom`)  
**Epistemic discipline:** every claim is tagged  
`[TEOREMA]` · `[CONJETURA]` · `[OPERACIONAL]` · `[INTERPRETACIÓN FÍSICA]` · `[AFIRMACIÓN ONTOLÓGICA]`  

**Scope.** This module confronts the discrete temporal progression generated by the Relational Extramental Discrete Clock (RECD) with the continuous time parameter of classical nonequilibrium thermodynamics. It contains definitions, structural incompatibility axes, intermediate bridge operators, formal confrontation statements, a reformulation of the second law in RECD variables, and an open-problem agenda. Empirical series (Aedes, Holter, finance, etc.) are excluded from mathematical statements.

**Non-mixing rule.** No claim of one epistemic level is used to discharge a claim of another level.

---

## 0. Fixed operational law (input, non-negotiable)

**[OPERACIONAL]** The reference RECD tick used in this module is the Lean-aligned skeleton

\[
\Delta t_k \;=\; g(\tau_s^{(k)}) \cdot \delta^{-k} \cdot \lvert \tau_s^{(k)} \rvert,
\]

where:

- \(\tau_s^{(k)} \in \mathbb{Q}\) (or \(\mathbb{R}\) in continuum lifts) is the Systemic Tau value at discrete index \(k\);
- \(g\) is the verified piecewise gate (values \(+1\), \(-1\), \(0\), or graded on the chaotic band);
- \(\delta > 1\) is the operational Feigenbaum constant (rational lab approximation \(\delta_{\mathrm{op}}\) in Lean; real \(\delta_{\mathrm{Feig}}\) in continuum statements);
- \(k \in \mathbb{N}\) is the renormalization / chaotic-run depth index (not wall-clock time).

**[OPERACIONAL]** Reference gate law (Lean `SystemicTau.gate`):

\[
g(\tau) \;=\;
\begin{cases}
+1 & \text{if }\tau \ge \tau_{\mathrm{st}},\\[0.25em]
\dfrac{\delta-1}{\delta}\cdot\dfrac{\tau_{\mathrm{ch}}-\lvert\tau\rvert}{\tau_{\mathrm{ch}}}
  & \text{if }\lvert\tau\rvert < \tau_{\mathrm{ch}},\\[0.75em]
-1 & \text{if }\tau \le -\tau_{\mathrm{ch}},\\[0.25em]
0 & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]

with operational thresholds \(\tau_{\mathrm{st}} = 1/2\), \(\tau_{\mathrm{ch}} = 41/100\).

**[TEOREMA]** (discharged in Lean) On the open chaotic band \(\lvert\tau\rvert < \tau_{\mathrm{ch}}\), \(g\) depends only on \(\lvert\tau\rvert\); on the nonnegative chaotic half-band \(g\) is antitone; stable classification forces \(g=+1\); anti-sync classification forces \(g=-1\); intermediate nonnegative band \(\tau_{\mathrm{ch}}\le\tau<\tau_{\mathrm{st}}\) forces \(g=0\). (Sources: `gate_chaos_abs_formula`, `gate_antitone_on_nonneg_chaos`, `gate_of_stable`, `gate_of_antiSync`, `gate_intermediate_nonneg`.)

**[OPERACIONAL]** Asymmetry: the law is **not** globally odd/even. Anti-sync opens \(g=-1\) for all \(\tau\le -\tau_{\mathrm{ch}}\), while the positive intermediate band keeps \(g=0\).

## 1. Formal dual definitions

### Definition 1.1 — RECD time generator

**[OPERACIONAL]** Fix a sequence of Systemic Tau samples \((\tau_s^{(k)})_{k\in\mathbb{N}}\) and a depth schedule \((k_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\) with \(k_n\in\mathbb{N}\) (in the unit skeleton one may take \(k_n = n\), or a run-depth counter; the distinction is operational, not ontological).

1. **Tick (increment).**  
   \[
   \Delta T_n \;:=\; g\bigl(\tau_s^{(n)}\bigr)\cdot \delta^{-k_n}\cdot \lvert \tau_s^{(n)}\rvert.
   \]
   (When \(k_n = n\) this is exactly the Lean `recdTick_unit`.)

2. **Accumulation (partial sums).**  
   \[
   T_0 := 0,\qquad
   T_{n+1} := T_n + \Delta T_n,\qquad
   T_n = \sum_{m=0}^{n-1}\Delta T_m.
   \]

3. **Regime dependence.** Let \(\mathrm{classify}(\tau_s^{(n)})\in\{\mathrm{stable},\mathrm{chaotic},\mathrm{antiSync},\mathrm{intermediate}\}\) be the operational partition of Thresholds. Then the sign and magnitude of \(\Delta T_n\) are regime-dependent through \(g\) and \(\lvert\tau_s\rvert\), and the scale \(\delta^{-k_n}\) is depth-dependent.

4. **RECD clock path.** The discrete path is the sequence
   \[
   \gamma^{\mathrm{RECD}} \;=\; \bigl(n,\, T_n,\, \tau_s^{(n)},\, k_n\bigr)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}
   \;\in\;
   \bigl(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{N}\bigr)^{\mathbb{N}}.
   \]

**[TEOREMA]** (elementary, definitional) \(\Delta T_n \in \mathbb{R}\) for all \(n\); the map \(n\mapsto T_n\) is a real sequence; it need not be monotone (because \(g\) may be negative).

**[INTERPRETACIÓN FÍSICA]** \(T_n\) is an event-driven accumulator of filtered ordinal reorganization mass. It is not identified with laboratory seconds.

**[AFIRMACIÓN ONTOLÓGICA]** (optional reading, not used below) Identifying \(T_n\) with “extramental discrete time” is a philosophical thesis at Level L3; the confrontation mathematics of this module lives at Levels L1–L2 and does not discharge L3.

---

### Definition 1.2 — Classical thermodynamic time generator

**[OPERACIONAL]** (standard continuum thermodynamics, fixed as comparison object)

1. **Absolute time parameter.** A continuous parameter \(t\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\), extrinsic to the state: the evolution is written as a curve \(x:[0,\infty)\to X\) on a state space \(X\) (manifold, Banach space, or finite-dimensional simplex).

2. **Evolution semigroup.** A (typically strongly continuous) semigroup \((P_t)_{t\ge 0}\) acting on observables or densities,
   \[
   P_{t+s} = P_t\circ P_s,\qquad P_0 = \mathrm{Id},
   \]
   so that the time parameter is additive and absolute.

3. **Monotonicity of the parameter.** The map \(t\mapsto t\) is strictly increasing; physical clocks advance only in the \(+t\) direction. Reverse trajectories, when considered, are reparametrizations of a **different** process, not negative increments of the same absolute \(t\).

4. **Entropy production.** For a thermodynamic process with total entropy \(S\) and entropy flux \(d_e S\), the internal production rate satisfies the classical second-law inequality
   \[
   \sigma_{\mathrm{cl}}(t) \;:=\; \frac{d_i S}{dt}\;\ge\; 0
   \]
   along admissible evolutions (Clausius–Duhem / local entropy balance in continuum thermodynamics; Schnakenberg form on Markov jump networks).

**[TEOREMA]** (classical textbook) Under the standard axioms of continuum thermodynamics with a single absolute time, \(\sigma_{\mathrm{cl}}\ge 0\) is a constraint on admissible processes, not a definition of \(t\).

**[INTERPRETACIÓN FÍSICA]** Classical \(t\) is the independent variable of the balance laws; it is not generated by ordinal correlations among measured channels.

---

### Definition 1.3 — Trajectory spaces of both models

**[OPERACIONAL]**

**A. RECD trajectory space.**  
Let \(\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{RECD}}\) be the set of sequences
\[
\gamma = \bigl(\tau_s^{(n)},\, k_n,\, \Delta T_n,\, T_n\bigr)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}
\]
such that \(\Delta T_n = g(\tau_s^{(n)})\,\delta^{-k_n}\,\lvert\tau_s^{(n)}\rvert\) and \(T_{n+1}=T_n+\Delta T_n\), \(T_0=0\). Equip \(\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{RECD}}\) with the product topology of pointwise convergence (or, when needed, the metric \(d(\gamma,\gamma')=\sum_n 2^{-n}\min\bigl(1,\lvert T_n-T_n'\rvert+\lvert\tau_s^{(n)}-\tau_s'^{(n)}\rvert\bigr)\)).

**B. Classical thermodynamic trajectory space.**  
Let \(\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{th}}\) be the set of absolutely continuous (or càdlàg, for jump processes) curves
\[
x:[0,\infty)\to X
\]
together with an entropy production density \(\sigma_{\mathrm{cl}}\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}([0,\infty))\) satisfying \(\sigma_{\mathrm{cl}}\ge 0\) a.e. Equip \(\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{th}}\) with the topology of uniform convergence on compact time intervals (or Skorokhod topology for jumps).

**C. Coupled observation.** When a multivariate continuous process \(Y_t\) generates windowed \(\tau_s\) estimates, one obtains a map from a subset of \(\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{th}}\) into sequences \((\tau_s^{(n)})\), hence into \(\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{RECD}}\) once a depth schedule is fixed. That map is the projection \(\pi\) of §3.

## 2. Confrontation table (structural incompatibilities)

The following axes are **structural**, not empirical. Each row identifies a property that holds for one generator and fails, or holds only conditionally, for the other.

| Axis | RECD generator \(T_n\) | Classical thermodynamic \(t\) | Incompatibility type |
|------|------------------------|-------------------------------|----------------------|
| **Continuity vs discreteness** | Time advances by countable ticks \(\Delta T_n\); path is a step path in the accumulant | Time is a continuous (or dense) parameter of a flow/semigroup | **Ontological/structural of parameter type** |
| **Monotonicity of the time parameter** | \(T_{n+1}-T_n=\Delta T_n\) may be \(>0\), \(=0\), or \(<0\) (via \(g=-1\)) | \(t\) is strictly monotone nondecreasing along physical evolution; negative \(dt\) is not an admissible clock increment | **Global sign structure** |
| **Origin of the parameter** | Generated by ordinal correlations \(\tau_s\) and regime gate \(g\); intrinsic to the relational series | Extrinsic absolute parameter of the balance laws; independent of Kendall-type concordance | **Genesis of time** |
| **Renormalization by \(\delta^{-k}\)** | Depth \(k\) multiplies the tick by \(\delta^{-k}\); chaotic runs densify the intrinsic clock | Standard continuum thermo has no Feigenbaum depth factor in \(dt\) | **Scale structure** |
| **Negative increments** | Possible whenever \(g(\tau_s)<0\) with \(\lvert\tau_s\rvert>0\) (anti-sync band) | Classical \(dt>0\); entropy production uses positive orientation of \(t\) | **Orientation** |
| **Null ticks** | Possible when \(g=0\) (intermediate nonnegative band) or \(\tau_s=0\) | \(dt\) does not freeze because of ordinal band membership | **Idling policy** |
| **Semigroup law** | \((T_n)\) is a discrete walk; composition is addition of ticks, not a continuous semigroup in \(t\) | \(P_{t+s}=P_t P_s\) on the continuum parameter | **Algebra of evolution** |
| **Entropy carrier** | No classical \(\sigma_{\mathrm{cl}}\) is part of Def. 1.1; ordinal production \(\sigma_{\mathrm{RECD}}\) must be **defined** (Prop. CT-4) | \(\sigma_{\mathrm{cl}}=d_iS/dt\ge 0\) is primitive | **Second-law carrier** |

**[TEOREMA]** (elementary from Def. 1.1 and the gate law) There exist sequences \((\tau_s^{(n)})\) with \(\Delta T_n < 0\) for infinitely many \(n\) (take \(\tau_s^{(n)}\le -\tau_{\mathrm{ch}}\) constantly). Hence global monotonicity of \(T_n\) is **not** a theorem of the RECD generator alone.

**[TEOREMA]** (classical) Global monotonicity of \(t\) **is** part of the classical thermodynamic time generator as fixed in Def. 1.2.

**Corollary (structural non-identity).**  
**[TEOREMA]** The identity map of parameters “\(T_n \equiv t\)” is not an isomorphism of generators: one admits negative increments and discrete null ticks with \(\delta\)-renormalization; the other does not.

## 3. Intermediate constructions (bridges)

### 3.1 Immersion operator \(\iota\)

**[OPERACIONAL]** An **immersion** maps a RECD sequence into a continuous path so that continuum tools (semigroups, entropy densities) can be applied without pretending the generators are identical.

**Definition (Immersion \(\iota\)).**  
Fix a chronological mesh \((s_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\) with \(s_0=0\), \(s_{n+1}>s_n\), \(\lim_{n\to\infty}s_n=\infty\) (e.g. \(s_n = n\cdot h\) for mesh size \(h>0\), or \(s_n = \sum_{m<n}\lvert\Delta T_m\rvert + n\varepsilon\) if one wants to avoid total stall). Define \(\iota:\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{RECD}}\to C([0,\infty),\mathbb{R})\) (or BV / piecewise linear paths) by linear interpolation of the accumulant on each chronological interval:

\[
\bigl(\iota(\gamma)\bigr)(s)
\;=\;
T_n + \frac{s-s_n}{s_{n+1}-s_n}\,(T_{n+1}-T_n)
\quad\text{for } s\in[s_n,s_{n+1}],
\]

and, if a state path is required, pair this with a piecewise-constant or linearly interpolated state \(x(s)\) carrying the window used to estimate \(\tau_s^{(n)}\).

**Properties (stated carefully):**

- **[TEOREMA]** \(\iota(\gamma)\) is continuous and piecewise \(C^0\); on each open interval \((s_n,s_{n+1})\) it is affine with slope \(\dfrac{\Delta T_n}{s_{n+1}-s_n}\).  
  **Lean (discrete \(\mathbb{Q}\) skeleton):** `meshTime`, `immerseNode`, `immerseAffine`, `immerseSlope` in `RECD_Immersion.lean`. Full \(C([0,\infty),\mathbb{R})\) path type remains optional.
- **[TEOREMA]** If \(\Delta T_n\ge 0\) for all \(n\) and \(s_n\) is strictly increasing, then \(s\mapsto (\iota\gamma)(s)\) is nondecreasing.  
  **Lean:** `immerseAffine_mono_of_tick_nonneg`, `immerseSlope_nonneg_of_tick_nonneg`; horizon mono via CT-3.
- **[TEOREMA]** If some \(\Delta T_n<0\), then \(\iota\gamma\) is **not** monotone, even though the chronological mesh \(s_n\) is.  
  **Lean:** `immerseAffine_not_mono_of_neg_tick`, `immerseAffine_strict_anti_of_neg_tick` (`RECD_CT2`); sample `recdAccum_constAntiSync_strict_anti_monotone`.
- **[OPERACIONAL]** Choice of mesh \((s_n)\) is a convention; different meshes yield different immersions. Any continuum comparison must declare the mesh.

**Remark.** Immersion does **not** create a classical thermodynamic entropy production; it only embeds the RECD accumulant as a continuous path.

---

### 3.2 Projection operator \(\pi\)

**[OPERACIONAL]** A **projection** extracts ordinal structure and an RECD path from a continuous multivariate trajectory.

**Definition (Projection \(\pi\)).**  
Let \(Y:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}^d\) be a continuous (or càdlàg) multivariate process, \(d\ge 2\). Fix:

- a window length \(W\in\mathbb{N}_{>0}\) (Lean `Window`);
- a chronological sampling grid \(t_n = n\cdot h\), \(h>0\);
- an estimator \(\widehat{\tau}_s\) of Systemic Tau on each window \(I_n = \{t_n-W+1,\ldots,t_n\}\) (mean pairwise Kendall on ranks);
- a depth rule \(k_n = K\bigl((\widehat{\tau}_s^{(m)})_{m\le n}\bigr)\) (e.g. length of current chaotic run).

Then
\[
\pi(Y)
\;=\;
\bigl(\widehat{\tau}_s^{(n)},\, k_n,\, \Delta T_n,\, T_n\bigr)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}
\;\in\;
\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{RECD}},
\]
with \(\Delta T_n = g(\widehat{\tau}_s^{(n)})\,\delta^{-k_n}\,\lvert\widehat{\tau}_s^{(n)}\rvert\).

**Properties:**

- **[OPERACIONAL]** \(\pi\) depends on \((W,h,\widehat{\tau}_s,K)\). Changing any of these changes the RECD path; this is measurement protocol, not a dynamical theorem.
- **[TEOREMA]** (structural) \(\pi\) is not injective: distinct continuous paths may share all windowed ordinal ranks and hence the same RECD path.
- **[TEOREMA]** (structural) \(\pi\circ\iota\) is not the identity on \(\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{RECD}}\) in general (immersion uses a mesh and interpolation; projection re-estimates \(\tau_s\) from a state lift that may not recover the original sequence).
- **[CONJETURA]** Under suitable mixing and window asymptotics, \(\widehat{\tau}_s^{(n)}\to \tau_s^{\star}(t_n)\) in probability for a population ordinal coupling \(\tau_s^{\star}\). (Estimator consistency; not discharged here.)

---

### 3.3 Controlled continuum limit

**[OPERACIONAL]** A **controlled continuum limit** is a regime in which the discrete RECD accumulant, after immersion, converges to a classical continuous clock (monotone absolutely continuous path) with a well-defined density.

**Definition (Controlled continuum limit).**  
Let \((\gamma^{(h)})_{h>0}\) be a family of RECD paths obtained by projecting a fixed continuous process \(Y\) at mesh \(h\), with depths \(k_n^{(h)}\) and ticks \(\Delta T_n^{(h)}\). Write \(T^{(h)}(s) := (\iota_h\gamma^{(h)})(s)\) for a declared immersion mesh consistent with \(h\).

We say that \(\gamma^{(h)}\) admits a **controlled continuum limit** if there exists a nondecreasing absolutely continuous function \(T^{\infty}:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}\) such that:

1. \(T^{(h)}\to T^{\infty}\) uniformly on compact time intervals;
2. \(\dfrac{d}{ds}T^{\infty}(s) = v(s)\) a.e. for some \(v\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}\), \(v\ge 0\);
3. the gate remains in the nonnegative cone along the limit support: \(\liminf g(\widehat{\tau}_s^{(n,h)})\ge 0\) in a sense compatible with (1)–(2);
4. depths remain bounded or the series \(\sum_n \delta^{-k_n^{(h)}}\,\lvert\widehat{\tau}_s^{(n,h)}\rvert\) is controlled so that no pathological \(\delta\)-collapse occurs.

**Sufficient conditions (statement-level):**

**[CONJETURA] (CT-ContLim)** Assume:

- (H1) **Stable domination:** \(\widehat{\tau}_s^{(n,h)}\ge \tau_{\mathrm{st}}\) for all \(n\) large and all small \(h\) (gate \(g\equiv +1\));
- (H2) **Bounded depth:** \(k_n^{(h)}\le K_{\max}<\infty\) uniformly;
- (H3) **Regular sampling:** windows of length \(W\) on a process with uniformly continuous paths in probability;
- (H4) **Positive mass:** \(\inf_n \lvert\widehat{\tau}_s^{(n,h)}\rvert \ge c>0\) on the relevant range (or a weaker integral lower bound).

Then \(T^{(h)}\) converges (along a subsequence) to an absolutely continuous nondecreasing limit \(T^{\infty}\) with density proportional to a continuum interpolant of \(\lvert\tau_s\rvert\,\delta^{-k}\).

**Remark.** Conditions (H1)–(H2) deliberately exclude sustained anti-synchronization and unbounded chaotic-run depth. The continuum limit is therefore **conditional**, not universal.

**[TEOREMA]** (elementary obstruction; Lean `RECD_ContLim`) If \(g(\widehat{\tau}_s^{(n)})=-1\) for a set of indices with positive asymptotic density and \(\lvert\tau_s\rvert\) bounded away from zero, then no limit \(T^{\infty}\) can be nondecreasing. Hence (H1)-type control is essentially necessary for recovery of a classical clock orientation.  
Anchors: `contLim_obstruction_of_InfOftenAntiSync`, `contLim_obstruction_of_lowerDensity`.

**Discharged scaffold (Lean `RECD_ContLim`, 0 sorry).**

- H1–H4 as discrete `Prop`s + `ContLimHypotheses` bundle.
- Equi-Lipschitz of immersion cells under stable frozen depth + amp. upper bound (`contLim_equiLipschitz`).
- Exact linear continuum shape + Real `Tendsto atTop` for const-stable sample (`constStable_matches_linear`, `constStableAccumReal_tendsto_atTop`, `constStable_contLimNode`).
- Mesh refinement endpoint/midpoint consistency.

**Open residual.** Uniform-on-compacts convergence of immersed paths for general projected continuous processes under (H1)–(H4).

### Statement CT-1 — Local equivalence in stable regime

**Name.** Local equivalence of RECD accumulation and classical oriented time in the stable regime.

**[TEOREMA]** (discrete skeleton discharged in Lean: `SystemicTau.RECD_CT1`)  
**Hypotheses.**

1. \(\tau_s^{(n)}\ge \tau_{\mathrm{st}}\) for all \(n\) in a discrete interval \(N\in\{n_0,\ldots,n_1\}\) (hence \(g\equiv +1\) by Lean `gate_of_stable`).
2. Depth is frozen: \(k_n = k_\star\) constant on \(N\).
3. Immersion mesh is uniform: \(s_{n+1}-s_n = h>0\).
4. Comparison object: classical time restricted to an interval \(I\subset\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\) of length \(h\cdot\lvert N\rvert\).

**Claim.** On \(N\),  
\[
\Delta T_n = \delta^{-k_\star}\,\lvert\tau_s^{(n)}\rvert = \delta^{-k_\star}\,\tau_s^{(n)},
\]
the path \(n\mapsto T_n\) is nondecreasing, and the immersed path \(\iota\gamma\) is Lipschitz with nonnegative slope. After affine reparametrization \(u = c\cdot T_n\) with \(c>0\), the oriented parameter \(u\) is locally equivalent (order-isomorphic and bi-Lipschitz on compact subintervals where \(\tau_s\) is bounded above and below by positive constants) to classical time \(t\) on \(I\).

**Discharged in Lean (exact \(\tau_s\), finite horizon).**

- **[TEOREMA]** \(\tau\ge\tau_{\mathrm{st}}\Rightarrow g(\tau)=1\) and \(\Delta T_n=\delta^{-k}\tau_n\ge\delta^{-k}\tau_{\mathrm{st}}>0\).  
  Anchors: `recdTick_unit_of_stable`, `recdTick_unit_pos_of_stable`, `recdTick_unit_stable_bounds`.
- **[TEOREMA]** Strict monotonicity and order embedding \(i\le j\Rightarrow T_i\le T_j\), \(i<j\Rightarrow T_i<T_j\).  
  Anchors: `recdAccum_strictMono_of_stable`, `recdAccum_le_of_le_stable`, `recdAccum_lt_of_lt_stable`.
- **[TEOREMA]** Amplitude sandwich \(m\le\tau\le M\Rightarrow n\cdot\delta^{-k}m\le T_n\le n\cdot\delta^{-k}M\).  
  Anchor: `recdAccum_stable_sandwich`.
- **[TEOREMA]** Discrete bi-Lipschitz of \(n\mapsto T_n\) with \(\ell=\delta^{-k}m\), \(L=\delta^{-k}M\) (\(m>0\)).  
  Anchor: `recdAccum_stable_biLipschitz`.
- **[TEOREMA]** Mesh form: \(\ell\cdot(s_b-s_a)\le T_b-T_a\le L\cdot(s_b-s_a)\) with \(\ell=\delta^{-k}m/h\), \(L=\delta^{-k}M/h\).  
  Anchor: `recdAccum_stable_biLipschitz_mesh`.
- Sample: constant stable \(\tau\equiv 3/4\) yields \(T_n=n\cdot(3/4)\).  
  Anchor: `recdAccum_constStable_exact`.

**What remains open.** Full bi-Lipschitz equivalence after projection noise, and semigroup intertwining \(P_t \leftrightarrow\) discrete tick composition, under realistic estimators \(\widehat{\tau}_s\).

### Statement CT-2 — Global non-equivalence under sustained anti-synchronization

**Name.** Global non-equivalence of RECD time and classical thermodynamic time under sustained anti-sync.

**[TEOREMA]** (elementary half discharged in Lean: `SystemicTau.RECD_CT2`)  
**[CONJETURA]** residual: categorical non-existence of orientation-preserving intertwining with continuum semigroups (claim 3–4 structure).

**Hypotheses.**  
There exists an infinite set \(A\subset\mathbb{N}\) of asymptotic density \(d>0\) such that \(\tau_s^{(n)}\le -\tau_{\mathrm{ch}}\) for all \(n\in A\) (hence \(g=-1\)), and \(\inf_{n\in A}\lvert\tau_s^{(n)}\rvert \ge c>0\).

**Claim.**  
1. \(\Delta T_n \le -c\cdot\delta^{-k_n}<0\) for all \(n\in A\).  
2. The sequence \((T_n)\) is **not** eventually nondecreasing (classical clock orientation fails); on mixed-sign sustained samples it is not eventually monotone either.  
3. There is no order-embedding \(\Phi:\mathrm{range}(T_n)\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\) that both (i) preserves the generator’s increment orientation for all large \(n\) and (ii) intertwines with a classical thermodynamic semigroup parameterized by absolute \(t\).  
4. Consequently, RECD time and classical thermodynamic time are **globally non-equivalent** as oriented generators on any trajectory class containing sustained anti-sync.

**Discharged fragment (Lean, 0 sorry).**

- **[TEOREMA]** Anti-sync + \(\lvert\tau\rvert\ge c>0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(\Delta T\le -c\cdot\delta^{-k}<0\).  
  Anchors: `recdTick_unit_antiSync_le_neg`, `absRat_ge_tauChaos_of_antiSync`.
- **[TEOREMA]** Infinitely often anti-sync \(\Rightarrow\) \(T\) not eventually nondecreasing.  
  Anchors: `InfOftenAntiSync`, `not_eventually_nondecreasing_of_InfOftenAntiSync`.
- **[TEOREMA]** Positive lower density \(d\cdot N\le\#\)anti-sync \(\Rightarrow\) InfOften + not eventually nondecreasing.  
  Anchors: `HasAntiSyncLowerDensity`, `InfOftenAntiSync_of_lowerDensity`, `not_eventually_nondecreasing_of_lowerDensity`.
- **[TEOREMA]** Frozen depth + density + amp. floor \(\Rightarrow\) reverse mass grows at least linearly.  
  Anchors: `negVarAccum_ge_antiSync_mass`, `negVarAccum_ge_linear_of_density`.
- **[TEOREMA]** Immersion on a negative-tick cell is not nondecreasing in \(\theta\).  
  Anchors: `immerseAffine_not_mono_of_neg_tick`, `immerseAffine_strict_anti_of_neg_tick`.
- **Samples.** Constant anti-sync (density 1); period-2 anti/stable (density \(1/2\), \(T_{2m}=0\), \(T_{2m+1}=-3/4\), neither eventually nondec. nor noninc.).  
  Anchors: `constAntiSync_*`, `period2AntiSync_not_eventually_monotone`, `recdAccum_period2_*`.

### Statement CT-3 — Recovery of monotonicity

**Name.** Monotonicity recovery criteria for \(T_n\).

**[TEOREMA]** (discharged in Lean: `SystemicTau.RECD_Monotonicity`)  
Let \((\tau_s^{(n)},k_n)\) generate \(\Delta T_n = g(\tau_s^{(n)})\,\delta^{-k_n}\,\lvert\tau_s^{(n)}\rvert\). Then the following are equivalent for a fixed horizon \(N\):

1. \(T_{n+1}\ge T_n\) for all \(n<N\);
2. \(\Delta T_n \ge 0\) for all \(n<N\);
3. \(g(\tau_s^{(n)})\ge 0\) for all \(n<N\) with \(\tau_s^{(n)}\ne 0\).

**Lean anchors.** `recdAccum_monotone_iff_ticks`, `recdAccum_monotone_iff_gate`, `recdTick_unit_nonneg_iff_gate`.

**[TEOREMA]** (discharged) Under the reference law, **\(g(\tau)<0\) if and only if \(\tau\le -\tau_{\mathrm{ch}}\)**.

and a uniform amplitude bound \(\lvert\tau_s^{(n)}\rvert\le B\) for all \(n<N\), the reverse mass satisfies

\sum_{n<N}\Delta T_n^{-} \;\le\; B\cdot M,
\]
hence \(T_N\ge T_0 - B\cdot M\). In the unit case \(B=1\) this is \(T_N\ge -M\).  
Depth need not be capped separately: \(\delta^{-k}\le 1\) for every \(k\) (operational \(\delta>1\)), so the worst reverse tick under \(\lvert\tau\rvert\le B\) has size \(B\).

### Statement CT-4 — Ordinal entropy production and classical entropy production

**Name.** Relation between \(\sigma_{\mathrm{RECD}}\) and \(\sigma_{\mathrm{cl}}\).

**Definition (ordinal entropy production).** **[OPERACIONAL]**  
Define the **forward ordinal mass** and **backward ordinal mass** of a tick by
\[
\Delta T_n^{+} := \max(\Delta T_n,0),\qquad
\Delta T_n^{-} := \max(-\Delta T_n,0),
\]
and the **ordinal entropy production increment**
\[
\Sigma_n^{\mathrm{RECD}}
\;:=\;
\Delta T_n^{+} + \alpha\,\Delta T_n^{-}
\;=\;
\begin{cases}
\Delta T_n & \text{if }\Delta T_n\ge 0,\\
-\alpha\,\Delta T_n & \text{if }\Delta T_n<0,
\end{cases}
\]
with a fixed asymmetry parameter \(\alpha\in[0,1]\) (default \(\alpha=1\) yields total variation contribution of negative ticks; \(\alpha=0\) ignores reverse ticks).  
**Sign note.** The case form forces the **plus** combination \(\Delta T^{+}+\alpha\Delta T^{-}\) (not minus): when \(\Delta T_n<0\), \(\Delta T_n^{-}=-\Delta T_n>0\) and \(\Sigma_n=-\alpha\Delta T_n=\alpha\Delta T_n^{-}\ge 0\). An informal “minus” writeup would contradict nonnegativity-by-construction. The cumulative production is
\[
\Sigma_N^{\mathrm{RECD}} := \sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\Sigma_n^{\mathrm{RECD}}.
\]
When an immersion mesh \((s_n)\) is fixed, set
\[
\sigma_{\mathrm{RECD}}(s)
\;:=\;
\frac{\Sigma_{n+1}^{\mathrm{RECD}}-\Sigma_n^{\mathrm{RECD}}}{s_{n+1}-s_n}
\quad\text{for }s\in(s_n,s_{n+1}),
\]
so \(\sigma_{\mathrm{RECD}}\ge 0\) by construction for any \(\alpha\in[0,1]\).

**Proposition CT-4A (nonnegativity by construction).**  
**[TEOREMA]** For every RECD path and every \(\alpha\in[0,1]\), \(\Sigma_N^{\mathrm{RECD}}\ge 0\) and \(\sigma_{\mathrm{RECD}}\ge 0\) almost everywhere on the immersion mesh.  
**Lean.** Cumulative half: `ordinalSigmaAccum_nonneg` (`RECD_OrdinalEntropy`). Mesh density half: uniform mesh \(s_n=n\cdot h\), density \(\sigma_n=\Sigma(\Delta T_n;\alpha)/h\), and `sigmaRECD_nonneg` on every cell (`RECD_Immersion`). Discrete a.e. = every open mesh cell.

**Proposition CT-4B (stable regime reduction).**  
**[TEOREMA]** If \(g\ge 0\) on the whole horizon, then \(\Delta T_n^{-}=0\), hence \(\Sigma_N^{\mathrm{RECD}} = T_N - T_0\), and \(\sigma_{\mathrm{RECD}}\) coincides with the density of the immersed accumulant.  
**Lean.** `ordinalSigmaAccum_eq_recdAccum_of_gate_nonneg`; mesh form `sigmaRECD_eq_immerseSlope_of_gate_nonneg`.

**Proposition CT-4C (comparison scheme with classical production).**  
**[CONJETURA]**  
Let \(Y_t\) be a continuous-time Markov jump process with Schnakenberg entropy production rate \(\sigma_{\mathrm{cl}}(t)\ge 0\). Let \(\pi(Y)\) be its RECD projection. Then there exist protocol-dependent constants \(C_{\pm}>0\) and a remainder \(R_N\) such that, on horizons where anti-sync density is at most \(\varepsilon\),
\[
C_{-}\int_0^{t_N}\sigma_{\mathrm{cl}}(t)\,dt - R_N(\varepsilon)
\;\le\;
\Sigma_N^{\mathrm{RECD}}
\;\le\;
C_{+}\int_0^{t_N}\sigma_{\mathrm{cl}}(t)\,dt + R_N(\varepsilon).
\]
No claim is made that \(\sigma_{\mathrm{RECD}}=\sigma_{\mathrm{cl}}\). Equality of carriers is false in general: \(\sigma_{\mathrm{RECD}}\) is ordinal and gate-filtered; \(\sigma_{\mathrm{cl}}\) is generated by probability currents on edges of the state graph.

**[INTERPRETACIÓN FÍSICA]** \(\sigma_{\mathrm{RECD}}\) measures production of **oriented ordinal reorganization mass**, not Clausius heat over temperature. Any identification with thermodynamic entropy is a modelling hypothesis, not a theorem.

**[AFIRMACIÓN ONTOLÓGICA]** (explicitly not used as a premise) Elevating \(\sigma_{\mathrm{RECD}}\) to “the” physical entropy production of nature is outside the mathematical confrontation.

## 5. Reformulation of the second law in RECD variables

### 5.1 Classical statement (reference)

**[TEOREMA]** (classical) For an isolated system, \(dS/dt = \sigma_{\mathrm{cl}}\ge 0\). For open systems, \(dS = d_e S + d_i S\) with \(d_i S/dt=\sigma_{\mathrm{cl}}\ge 0\).

### 5.2 Ordinal discrete second law (RECD form)

**Definition (regime change).** **[OPERACIONAL]**  
A **regime change** at index \(n\) is the event
\[
\rho_n := \mathbf{1}\bigl\{\mathrm{classify}(\tau_s^{(n)}) \ne \mathrm{classify}(\tau_s^{(n-1)})\bigr\},
\quad n\ge 1.
\]
Write \(R_N := \sum_{n=1}^{N-1}\rho_n\) for the number of regime changes up to \(N\).

**Statement SL-RECD (ordinal second law).**  
**[OPERACIONAL]** as a definitional inequality; **[CONJETURA]** as a physical law of nature.

> **SL-RECD.** Along any RECD path generated by the reference law,
> \[
> \Sigma_N^{\mathrm{RECD}}
> \;=\;
> \sum_{n=0}^{N-1}
> \bigl(\Delta T_n^{+} + \alpha\,\Delta T_n^{-}\bigr)
> \;\ge\; 0
> \]
> for every \(N\), with \(\alpha\in[0,1]\) fixed by protocol. Moreover, the accumulation of **forward** mass is constrained by regime structure:
> \[
> \sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\Delta T_n^{+}
> \;=\;
> \sum_{n:\,g(\tau_s^{(n)})>0}
> g(\tau_s^{(n)})\,\delta^{-k_n}\,\lvert\tau_s^{(n)}\rvert,
> \]
> and anti-sync visits contribute only through the reverse term \(\Delta T_n^{-}\) (or are discarded if \(\alpha=0\)).

**Refined form (regime-aware).**  
**[OPERACIONAL]**  
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
&\Sigma_N^{\mathrm{RECD}}\ge 0,\\
&\Delta T_n = g(\tau_s^{(n)})\,\delta^{-k_n}\,\lvert\tau_s^{(n)}\rvert,\\
&g\text{ as in §0},\quad
T_N = \sum_{n<N}\Delta T_n,\\
&\text{regime changes }R_N\text{ recorded but not required for nonnegativity of }\Sigma.
\end{aligned}
}
\]

**Epistemic status (mandatory separation).**

| Reading | Label | Content |
|---------|-------|---------|
| \(\Sigma_N^{\mathrm{RECD}}\ge 0\) by construction of \(\Delta T^{\pm}\) | **[TEOREMA]** | Pure arithmetic |
| “Physical processes obey SL-RECD as their second law” | **[INTERPRETACIÓN FÍSICA]** / **[CONJETURA]** | Modelling claim |
| “SL-RECD is the ontological law of discrete extramental time” | **[AFIRMACIÓN ONTOLÓGICA]** | Not used in confrontation proofs |
| Classical \(\sigma_{\mathrm{cl}}\ge 0\) | **[TEOREMA]** (classical thermo) | Independent comparison object |

**Compatibility note.**  
When \(g\ge 0\) everywhere, SL-RECD reduces to \(T_N\ge T_0\), i.e. monotonicity of the RECD accumulant (Statement CT-3). When anti-sync occurs, SL-RECD keeps nonnegativity of **production** \(\Sigma\) while allowing the **clock** \(T_n\) to decrease — exactly the structural split forbidden in classical absolute time, where the parameter \(t\) itself cannot reverse.
